name: Vespid Dynamics Compound Eye Surveillance Cluster
product_name: Vespid Dynamics Compound Eye Surveillance Cluster
description: A deployable surveillance device consisting of 12 micro-cameras mounted on flexible stalks extending from a central hub, providing 360-degree visual coverage from a single mounting point. Each camera stalk can be independently positioned and focused, and the combined feed creates a composite image with no blind spots. The device adheres to surfaces with a gecko-pad base and draws power from an integrated solar cell, operating indefinitely in lit environments. The Compound Eye's individual cameras are each smaller than a shirt button, making the deployed device easy to overlook despite its multi-stalk profile.
story_hooks: A sweep of a Tier 3 apartment building discovered 40+ Compound Eye devices installed in hallways, stairwells, and common areas — someone has been running total surveillance on the building's residents for months.
A Compound Eye device was found inside a corporate boardroom that had been transmitting to a receiver outside the building — the device had been in place for six weeks without detection.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Gecko Ascender GA-4

physical_description.visual_profile: A biomimetic surveillance hub resembling a mechanical sea anemone or insect compound eye. Central disc (roughly coin-sized) from which 12 articulated stalks radiate outward like organic appendages. Each stalk terminates in a lens no larger than a shirt button. Overall impression is deliberately organic yet clearly synthetic—nature-inspired industrial design.
physical_description.dimensions: Central hub: 2.5 cm diameter. Fully deployed with stalks extended: ~8 cm spherical footprint. Stalk length: 3 cm each.
physical_description.weight_description: 40 grams total—pocketable, weighs less than a smartphone. So light it requires minimal surface adhesion pressure.
physical_description.primary_material: Central hub: brushed titanium-composite with carbon fiber reinforcement. Stalks: flexible polymer with embedded microfiber optics and servo actuators. Lens elements: hardened synthetic sapphire.
physical_description.finish: Satin gunmetal on hub with iridescent oil-slick patina where light catches the stalk joints (effect of multi-layer anti-reflective coating). Stalks have subtle segmentation marks from servo articulation points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey central hub with gunmetal accents. Stalks fade to matte black at their tips. Lens elements catch ambient light with faint emerald bloom from AR coatings.
physical_description.interface_elements: Minimal physical interface: small recessed touch-capacitive panel (1cm²) on hub's dorsal side for power/mode selection. Trio of micro-LEDs (power, link status, battery) emit in soft cyan. Micro USB-C port (recessed, covered) for emergency wired sync. No visible antenna—transmission handled via substrate.
distinctive_features: Stalks flex and articulate independently with minimal servo noise—sound is nearly inaudible mechanical whirring
Each stalk can rotate ~120° independently; cameras create overlapping composite with AI edge-blending
Gecko-pad base shows faint honeycomb microstructure under light; no adhesive residue when removed
Slight heat shimmer during solar charging—barely perceptible
When powered down, stalks droop naturally—mimics deflated organism state
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS logo (stylized wasp head in chrome relief) on hub's ventral side. Microscopic regulatory stamps: GLMZ Cert 2226, encryption standard notation (⊞ QT-256), solar efficiency rating. Serial number laser-etched on base.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deployed on corner of window frame, ceiling junction, or shelf edge—often barely visible until light hits the lens elements. Stalks at varying angles, creating organic asymmetrical silhouette. Faint dust accumulation on some lens caps after weeks of operation. Battery indicator dim but steady in low-light environments.
